name: Build the customer identity resolution and unified profile pipeline
what: Matches every record that names the same person, guest checkouts, repeat emails, phone and WhatsApp numbers, POS and marketplace orders, support tickets, loyalty and subscription accounts, into one profile, so segmentation, LTV and support context are not split across five half-profiles the way they are when each tool keeps its own record.
encompasses: Match records by email, phone (with country-code normalisation), and shipping address fuzzy match
Merge guest-checkout orders into the matching account once a match is confident, never silently for weak matches
Reconcile a WhatsApp business number against the checkout phone field where WhatsApp is used (common in India, EU, LATAM)
Fold POS and marketplace (Amazon, Walmart Marketplace, or Flipkart in India) orders into the same profile when a store also sells there
Attach support ticket history and review history to the resolved profile, not just order history
Flag low-confidence merges for a human to confirm rather than auto-merging
Expose one `customer_id` the segmentation model, loyalty tiering and churn score all key off
Keep an audit trail of every merge and split decision with the evidence used
Re-run resolution nightly as new orders and tickets arrive, not as a one-time project
outputs: a resolved customer_id table with merge confidence and evidence
a queue of low-confidence merges for human review
trigger: nightly batch, or on request when segmentation looks wrong
founder_sees: the merge queue and any large jump in unified-profile count after a rerun

name: Configure and govern the AI support agent's autonomous actions
what: Writes the operating procedures that decide exactly which support actions an AI agent (order status, address change, refund up to a cap, subscription pause) may take on its own, which need a human, and what triggers an escalation, then tests the agent against real past tickets before it goes live, rather than turning on a vendor's default and hoping.
encompasses: List every contact type the helpdesk sees and classify each as agent-can-close, agent-can-draft, or human-only
Write the rulebook (natural-language business rules plus the hard limits) for money-moving actions: refund cap, who can approve above it, which order states allow a refund at all
Set identity-verification steps before any account or payment change
Set escalation triggers: sentiment, repeated back-and-forth, explicit request for a human, ticket value above a threshold
Require a warm hand-off that carries full conversation history, never a cold restart with the human
Cover every channel the brand actually uses (email, chat, WhatsApp, Instagram DM), not just the vendor's default channel
Replay the agent against a sample of last quarter's real tickets before go-live and score accuracy and tone
Set a kill switch and a rollback plan if the agent starts producing wrong answers
Re-test after every policy or price change, since a stale rulebook is how an agent promises a refund the brand no longer offers
outputs: an operating-procedure document for the AI agent
trigger: before any AI support agent goes live, and after every policy change
founder_sees: the full operating-procedure document and the replay test scores before anything goes live

name: Build the post-purchase zero-party attribution survey
what: Designs the one-question, thank-you-page survey ("how did you hear about us") with branching by product or customer type, and turns the answers into a channel-share number the brand can compare against paid spend, catching word-of-mouth, influencer and offline channels that pixels miss. Distinct from the NPS/CSAT survey, which measures satisfaction, not discovery.
encompasses: Write the single first question and the branch questions for first-time vs returning buyers
Branch by product bought or geography where the answer would differ
Set the response-rate target and page placement (thank-you page beats a follow-up email)
Convert raw answers into a channel-share percentage in code, never in the model
Compare self-reported channel share against paid-channel spend to compute an implied cost per attributed order for channels pixels cannot see (podcast, influencer, word of mouth)
Run a lift check by comparing survey answers before and after a specific campaign
Feed the channel-share numbers into the media buyer specialist's channel mix decisions
Re-survey quarterly since word-of-mouth share drifts as paid mix changes
inputs: current paid channel spend by channel
existing NPS/CSAT survey if any, to avoid survey fatigue
outputs: a survey script with branching logic
a channel-share report tied to spend
trigger: building or refreshing the attribution model; a new high-spend channel needs proof it works
founder_sees: the survey question set and the channel-share report

name: Run third-party review and reputation management across marketplaces and public sites
what: Monitors and drafts responses to reviews and complaints that live off the brand's own site: Google Business Profile, marketplace reviews (Amazon, Walmart Marketplace, or Flipkart in India), and public complaint boards, which the brand's own review platform (Yotpo, Judge.me) does not see because it only captures on-site reviews.
encompasses: Pull new reviews and ratings from Google Business Profile on a schedule
Pull marketplace reviews for any marketplace the brand sells on
Check named public complaint boards for new mentions of the brand
Draft an honest, unfiltered response for each negative review, never a templated denial
Flag reviews that reveal a real product or fulfilment defect back to the brand brain, not just a canned reply
Never draft a response that offers anything a marketplace's terms forbid (Amazon and Google both forbid incentivising review removal)
Track average rating and volume over time per source, separate from the on-site review score
trigger: weekly, or when a rating drops sharply

external_write.surface: Google Business Profile / marketplace seller console

founder_sees: every drafted response before it posts, and the rating trend
human_role: CX manager / community manager for customers

name: Syndicate reviews and UGC into ads, product feed and marketplace listings
what: Takes reviews and photo/video UGC already collected on-site and pushes the strongest ones into the Google Shopping product feed, into ad creative as social proof, and into marketplace listing content, so review effort collected once pays out in more places than the product page.
encompasses: Rank reviews by usefulness (photo attached, specific detail, recency) rather than star rating alone
Select review star ratings and counts for the product feed so Shopping ads show rating stars
Pull the best review quotes into ad copy candidates for the paid-creative specialist, with the reviewer's permission basis noted
Push top reviews into marketplace listing content where the marketplace allows imported reviews
Never edit a review's wording; select and quote, do not rewrite
Refresh the selection quarterly as new reviews arrive
outputs: a review-quote bank for ad copy
trigger: product feed refresh, or a new ad concept needs proof
founder_sees: the selected review quotes and feed fields before publish
human_role: review platform manager / retention marketing manager

name: Build and moderate a branded customer community
what: Sets up and runs a branded Slack, Discord or Circle space for existing customers: channel structure, moderation policy, a light engagement calendar, and a route for community insight and complaints back into support and product, distinct from a support inbox because it is peer-to-peer and always on.
encompasses: Decide whether a community fits the brand at all (needs a base of repeat, high-engagement buyers; not every store benefits)
Choose the platform and design the channel/space structure
Write the moderation policy: what gets removed, how complaints in public channels get routed to support
Build a light always-on engagement calendar (prompts, early-access drops, AMAs) distinct from the campaign calendar
Set the rule for when a founder or team member should show up in person versus staying quiet
Route recurring themes from the community back to the brand brain and to the survey/VoC record
Track membership, active-member share and one proxy metric (repeat purchase rate of members vs non-members)
outputs: a community structure and moderation policy
trigger: founder decides to test a community; quarterly review after launch
founder_sees: the go/no-go recommendation, the structure and the moderation policy

name: Prepare and run the public complaint and social crisis-response playbook
what: Watches for a complaint about the brand gaining public traction (a viral post, a pile-on in comments, a consumer-forum thread) and has a pre-written response ladder ready: acknowledge fast, take detail offline, fix and report back, so the brand does not improvise its first public reply to a spreading complaint.
encompasses: Write the response ladder in advance: first-hour acknowledgement template, offline-handoff line, follow-up-after-fix line
Set the trigger for what counts as "going public" versus an ordinary single complaint
Decide who is authorised to reply publicly on the brand's behalf and who must approve first
Pre-agree the tone rule: no defensiveness, no deleting real complaints, no fake apology without a real fix
Log every public incident and its resolution so the pattern (same defect complained about twice) gets caught
Route a confirmed product or fulfilment defect straight to the brand brain and the returns/QA record
trigger: built once, used the moment a complaint starts spreading
founder_sees: every public reply before it posts, at least until the ladder is proven
human_role: CX manager / community manager for customers

name: Reconcile sales tax on returns and refunds
what: Checks that every completed return or refund correctly reverses the sales tax collected on the original order: state nexus rules, marketplace-facilitator tax already remitted by the marketplace, and resale-certificate exempt orders, since a refund that does not reverse tax overstates remitted liability and misstates 1099-K figures. India only: reconciles GST credit notes against returns and refunds instead, since a refund without a credit note overstates reported sales and lets the buyer claim input tax credit the seller never reversed; reads null for US brands.
encompasses: List every refunded/returned order in the period and check the sales-tax portion was correctly reversed or credited
Flag any refund where the tax adjustment is missing or was filed late against the filing deadline
Check whether a marketplace facilitator (Amazon, Walmart Marketplace) already remitted tax on the order, so the brand does not also refund tax it never collected
Exclude resale-certificate and other tax-exempt orders from the reconciliation, rather than treating them as a gap
Reconcile the tax-adjustment total against the refund total in the payment ledger, arithmetic in code

India only: check every refunded/returned order for a matching GST credit note, flag any missing or late credit note against the statutory deadline, and confirm credit notes go through the same e-invoice system as sales invoices where e-invoicing applies by turnover threshold; reads null for US brands
Hand the flagged list to accounts or the founder; this capability never files the return itself
inputs: tax-adjustment export from the invoicing/accounting system (Avalara/TaxJar, or the GST credit-note export for India)
sales-tax filing calendar (or GST filing calendar for India)
outputs: a reconciliation report of missing or late tax adjustments (GST credit notes for India)
trigger: monthly, before sales-tax filing (or GST return filing for India)
subagent: Lifecycle specialist (hands off to Money and ops for filing)
founder_sees: the reconciliation report

name: Monitor competitor and marketplace pricing over time
what: Tracks named competitors' and the brand's own marketplace listing prices over time, flagging material moves before the brand reacts, rather than pricing decisions being made on a one-off manual check.
encompasses: Track a named competitor list's prices on their own site and on shared marketplaces on a schedule
Track the brand's own price on each marketplace it sells on against its own site price
Flag a competitor price move above a set threshold, with date and evidence
Never recommend matching a competitor's price automatically; this is a signal, not a rule
Feed flagged moves into the offer/pricing specialist's next pricing review, not a live repricing engine
trigger: weekly, or before a scheduled pricing review
founder_sees: the flagged moves, not raw scrape data

name: Monitor MAP and price parity across marketplaces and resellers
what: Checks that the price shown for the brand's products matches the agreed minimum-advertised-price and stays consistent across the brand's own site, marketplaces and any reseller, so an unauthorised discounter does not undercut the brand's own channel and train buyers to shop elsewhere.
encompasses: List every channel and reseller the brand's products should appear on at an agreed price
Check each channel's live listing price on a schedule
Flag any channel below the agreed minimum, with a screenshot and date
Distinguish an honest one-off flash sale from a persistent violation
Hand violations to the founder for the actual enforcement conversation; this capability never contacts the reseller
trigger: weekly
founder_sees: the violation report with evidence

name: Design and manage the gift card program
what: Designs the store's own gift card offer as a product, not just a checkout field: denominations, expiry, corporate bulk-gifting terms, and how gift card balances interact with refunds and store credit, distinct from any single discount or GWP offer.
encompasses: Choose denominations and any bonus-value tier (buy $100, get $110 loaded)
Set expiry policy against what is legal in the brand's markets
Design a corporate/bulk-gifting offer for B2B or occasion buying
Decide how store credit issued for a return interacts with a purchased gift card (never expire a refund credit the way a promotional one might)
Model the float liability (unredeemed balance) so the founder sees the cash-flow effect
Write the gift card's own short flow: purchase confirmation, balance reminder before expiry, redemption receipt
inputs: current checkout/gift card app if any
trigger: founder wants a gift card offer, or the holiday/gifting calendar approaches
founder_sees: the full program design and the float model

name: Run proactive live-chat concierge outreach to high-intent and VIP visitors
what: Prepares and, where approved, triggers a proactive chat message to a visitor showing high buying intent (repeat visit to a high-AOV product, a known VIP returning to the site) rather than waiting for the visitor to open chat first, closer to a store associate approaching a browsing customer than an automated pop-up discount.
encompasses: Define the intent signals that qualify for proactive outreach (visit count, product viewed, known VIP status)
Write the opening line by signal, never a generic "need help?"
Set the cap on how often one visitor gets approached, to avoid feeling stalked
Route to a human live-chat agent immediately once the visitor replies; the agent only prepares the trigger and opener
Track conversion and reply rate by signal to prune openers that do not work
outputs: a proactive-chat trigger and opener set
trigger: building or refreshing the live-chat program
founder_sees: the trigger rules and openers before launch

name: Run phone-based concierge follow-up for high-value abandoners and inquiries
what: Prepares the call queue, script and outcome log for a human to phone a customer directly for a high-AOV cart abandonment or a pre-purchase question, the way a jewellery or considered-purchase brand's own staff would, rather than relying on email/SMS alone once the order value crosses a threshold.
encompasses: Set the AOV or product-category threshold above which a phone follow-up beats an email/SMS flow
Prepare the call script per scenario (cart abandon, pre-purchase question, VIP check-in)
Build the daily call queue ranked by order value and recency
Log call outcome and reason for no-sale back into the segmentation model
Never dial or record the call itself; a human places every call
inputs: cart abandonment data above the AOV threshold
trigger: daily, for a brand with a phone-concierge program (fits a luxury/considered-purchase brand)
founder_sees: the call queue and the outcome log

name: Draft a personalised, non-template win-back message per lapsed customer
what: For a customer flagged as lapsed, drafts one message that cites their actual last product, a plausible reason for lapsing drawn from their own support or review history, and a matched offer, instead of dropping every lapsed customer into the same win-back template. No vendor sells this per-customer draft today; every platform ships one win-back flow shared by a segment.
encompasses: Read the customer's last product, last support ticket (if any) and last review sentiment (if any)
Infer a plausible, evidence-based lapse reason (price, a bad support experience, product fit) rather than guessing
Draft one message addressing that specific reason with a matched, policy-compliant offer
Never fabricate a reason with no evidence; fall back to the standard segment flow when there is nothing to go on
Queue every draft for founder or team review before send; this is not an autonomous send
Track whether the personalised draft outperforms the standard win-back flow for the same segment
inputs: churn/lapse flag from the segmentation model
outputs: a per-customer win-back draft with the evidence it cites
trigger: a customer crosses the lapse threshold and has enough history to personalise from
founder_sees: every draft and the evidence behind it before send

name: Compute true customer profitability and feed it into segmentation and loyalty tiering
what: Adds support-ticket cost, return/refund cost, shipping cost and discount cost against each customer's revenue, in code, so VIP and loyalty tiering rewards the customers who are actually profitable rather than the ones who simply spend the most and cost the most to serve. No loyalty platform ties reward cost to measured cost-to-serve this directly today.
encompasses: Estimate a per-ticket support cost and attach it to the customers who filed tickets
Attach return/refund cost (product, shipping both ways, restocking) to the customer who returned
Attach discount cost actually redeemed, not list price, to each customer
Compute a profitability figure per customer, all arithmetic in code, never modelled by the model itself
Compare the profitability ranking against the revenue-only RFM ranking and flag the customers that move a lot
Feed the profitability figure into loyalty tier and VIP-treatment decisions as a second input, not a replacement for revenue
Show the founder both rankings side by side before any tiering change, since this reshuffles who counts as a VIP
inputs: support ticket volume and estimated cost
outputs: a comparison against the revenue-only ranking
trigger: quarterly, or before a loyalty tier redesign
founder_sees: both rankings side by side and the customers that move

name: Watch named competitor policy pages for material changes
what: Periodically reads named competitors' public returns, loyalty and subscription-terms pages and flags a material change (a longer free-return window, a new loyalty tier, a cheaper subscription cadence) with the date and a diff, so the brand reacts to a real competitive shift instead of matching blindly or missing it for months.
encompasses: Store a snapshot of each named competitor's returns, loyalty and subscription-terms page
Diff the current page against the last snapshot on a schedule
Filter out cosmetic changes and keep only material policy or term changes
Report the change with the date, the diff and why it might matter, never a recommendation to copy it
Feed a confirmed material change into the relevant capability (C26 for returns, C10 for loyalty, C43 for subscriptions) for the founder's actual decision
outputs: a dated change log with diffs
trigger: monthly
founder_sees: the change log, not raw page scrapes

name: Auto-reschedule failed deliveries through carrier self-service portals without an API
what: For a carrier with no API integration, an agent with browser access logs into the carrier's own self-service portal and rebooks a failed delivery (a USPS/UPS/FedEx delivery exception or return-to-sender) once the customer has confirmed a new date or address over SMS or email, work a smaller brand today does by hand because its carrier volume does not justify an API integration. India only: reschedules an NDR'd (non-delivery report) COD delivery once the customer confirms a new date over WhatsApp or SMS instead; reads null for US brands.
encompasses: Detect a failed-delivery event (a carrier exception or return-to-sender; an NDR for India's COD orders) from the carrier's tracking feed or webhook
Send the SMS or email reschedule prompt (WhatsApp is a market option for India) and capture the customer's chosen new date or corrected address
Log into the carrier's self-service portal and submit the reschedule with the confirmed date
Confirm the reschedule went through and update the order's expected delivery date
Escalate to a human the moment the portal requires a captcha, a manual call, or behaves unexpectedly
Never attempt this on a carrier where credentials are not the founder's own or where the portal forbids automation in its terms
inputs: carrier delivery-exception feed (an NDR feed for India)
customer's confirmed new delivery date or address
outputs: an escalation for anything the portal blocks
trigger: every delivery-exception (or NDR, for India) event, for carriers without an API
founder_sees: every reschedule attempt and every escalation

name: Design and run the outbound voice/IVR and click-to-call channel
what: Sets up voice as its own channel, separate from SMS, WhatsApp and push: automated IVR calls for pre-dispatch confirmation and satisfaction checks, and click-to-call for a VIP or high-AOV concierge conversation, since failed-delivery reduction and CX tooling often relies on voice alongside SMS (WhatsApp for India) and the brand's own channel rules do not currently cover it.
encompasses: Decide which use cases justify voice: order pre-dispatch confirmation (COD orders for India), delivery-failure follow-up, post-resolution satisfaction check, VIP concierge
Write the IVR script and call flow for each automated use case
Set the call-attempt cadence and quiet hours, matching the consent and quiet-hour rules already set for SMS/WhatsApp
Set click-to-call triggers for a human concierge conversation (from C60's high-AOV queue)
Log every call outcome (answered, confirmed, no answer, opted out) back into the order/customer record
Track cost per call against the ticket or failed-delivery deflection it produces (RTO deflection for India), so the channel earns its keep
trigger: building the voice channel, or extending it to a new use case
founder_sees: the scripts and the outcome/cost report

name: Handle data-subject access and erasure requests under CCPA and state privacy law
what: When a customer asks what personal data the brand holds or asks for it to be deleted, finds every system that holds that person's data (ESP, helpdesk, loyalty, subscription, POS), verifies identity, and responds inside the statutory window: an obligation under California's CCPA/CPRA and other state privacy laws (Virginia, Colorado and others) that sits on top of ordinary unsubscribe handling. India only: the same obligation runs under India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act instead; reads null for US brands.
encompasses: Maintain a simple data-inventory map of which systems hold customer PII
Verify the requester's identity before acting on an access or erasure request
For an access request, compile what is held and where, in plain language
For an erasure request, check whether another law requires the brand to keep the record (tax, warranty) before deleting
Execute or hand off the deletion across every system on the inventory, not just the ESP unsubscribe
Use the applicable law's own response window (CCPA/CPRA: typically 45 days, extendable once; DPDP for India: per the Act's own timeline) rather than a single fixed number
Log every request and its resolution date against the statutory response window
Distinguish this from marketing consent/unsubscribe handling (C03), which covers opt-out of sends, not deletion of held data
inputs: the system inventory of where PII lives
outputs: a request log with resolution dates
trigger: a customer submits an access or erasure request

external_write.surface: every system holding the customer's PII

founder_sees: every request and its resolution before the statutory deadline

name: Run marketplace seller-support queues separate from the brand's own helpdesk
what: Manages Amazon, Walmart Marketplace and (in India) Flipkart/Myntra buyer-seller messages and A-to-Z-style guarantee claims inside each marketplace's own seller console, on that marketplace's own response clock (48 hours to answer a buyer message, about 72 hours to respond to a claim), distinct from the brand's own helpdesk queue and its own SLAs.
encompasses: Pull open buyer-seller messages and claims from each marketplace seller console on a schedule
Draft a response inside each marketplace's own response window, never missing the 48-hour buyer-message clock that itself triggers a claim right
Draft the claim response with the evidence the marketplace accepts (delivery proof, correspondence log)
Track claim rate and reason over time and flag a rising rate as a signal for the returns/fulfilment specialist
Keep this queue separate from the brand's own helpdesk tagging and reporting, since the SLA clocks and rules differ
outputs: drafted responses and claim replies within each marketplace's clock
trigger: continuous, for a brand selling on Amazon, Walmart Marketplace, or (in India) Flipkart/Myntra
subagent: Lifecycle specialist (shares evidence with Product and supply for 22-AMZ)
founder_sees: drafted responses before they post, and the claim-rate trend

name: EXTENSION: Add pre-dispatch confirmation, fraud/address risk scoring and automated failed-delivery recovery to the SMS/WhatsApp commerce program
what: The original capability designs SMS (and, where used, WhatsApp) cart recovery and order updates, plus COD-to-prepaid conversion for COD markets. Failed-delivery-reduction tooling (ShipStation/EasyPost address validation for the US; India's Shipway, ClickPost for RTO) shows the fuller workflow also needs pre-dispatch confirmation, a fraud/address risk score, and an automatic recovery sequence the moment a delivery fails, which the original scope did not cover.
encompasses: Trigger an OTP, SMS/WhatsApp or IVR confirmation before an order ships when the risk score calls for it, not only order-update messages after
Score each order's fraud/failed-delivery risk from address-validation history and order pattern (pincode-level delivery-success history for India's COD orders)
Route a high-risk order to a manual check or a card-only offer instead of shipping blind (a prepaid-only offer for India's COD orders)
Fire an automatic SMS/email/IVR sequence the moment a carrier logs a delivery exception or return-to-sender (WhatsApp/SMS/IVR for India's NDR), offering redelivery or an address fix
Tie any prepaid or card-only nudge's discount size to the actual failed-delivery cost it avoids (the RTO cost avoided, for India), not an arbitrary number

Report delivery-confirmation rate and return-to-sender rate as new numbers the original scope did not track. India only: also report COD confirmation rate and RTO rate by pincode; reads null for US brands
inputs: carrier delivery-exception feed (an NDR feed for India)
trigger: building or refreshing the SMS/WhatsApp commerce program
founder_sees: the risk-scoring rule and the recovery sequence before launch

name: EXTENSION: Add predictive next-order-date timing to replenishment and subscription messaging
what: The original capability builds replenishment and subscription messages on charge reminders and fixed cadence. Predictive-sending tools now time each customer's replenishment nudge off their own likely next-order date rather than a fixed interval, which the original scope did not include.
encompasses: Estimate each customer's likely next-order date from their own purchase interval, not the product's average use-up time alone
Move the replenishment nudge earlier or later per customer based on that estimate
Re-estimate after every actual order, since the interval drifts
Fall back to the fixed-cadence default for a customer with too little order history to estimate from
Report predicted-vs-actual accuracy so the founder can see whether prediction beats the fixed cadence
trigger: refreshing the replenishment/subscription messaging program
founder_sees: the accuracy report before the default cadence is replaced

name: EXTENSION: Add the multi-stage cancel-flow architecture and gamified non-monetary perks to the subscription offer design
what: The original capability designs the subscription value proposition, perk gating and a single cancel-flow save offer. Subscription platforms now build a four-stage cancel flow with per-stage save-rate analytics, and gamified perks (streaks, mystery rewards, surprise gifts) as a non-monetary reason to stay, neither of which the original scope specified.
encompasses: Build the cancel flow as four stages: a benefit reminder, an exit-reason survey, a reason-matched alternative (pause, swap, frequency change), then a conditional offer only if the earlier stages fail
Match the alternative and the offer to the stated cancellation reason and to the subscriber's order count/value, not one offer for everyone
Track save rate per stage so a weak stage can be rewritten instead of guessing which stage lost the subscriber
Design non-monetary retention mechanics (order streaks, a surprise gift at a milestone, a mystery reward) as an addition to, not a replacement for, the discount-based save offer
A/B test the gamified perk against a discount-only save to see which actually holds subscribers for this brand
inputs: subscriber order history and cancellation reasons
trigger: refreshing the subscription offer or cancel flow
founder_sees: the four-stage design and the per-stage save-rate results

name: EXTENSION: Add AI theme-clustering of open-text feedback and IVR-based post-resolution CSAT
what: The original capability runs the standing NPS/CSAT/VoC survey process. It did not include machine reading of open-ended survey, ticket and review text at scale to surface recurring themes without a human reading every response, or capturing CSAT immediately by phone right after a support case closes.
encompasses: Pool open-text answers from NPS/CSAT surveys, closed support tickets and reviews into one set for the period
Cluster them into named recurring themes with example quotes and a count per theme, not just a sentiment score
Flag a theme that is new this period or growing, separate from a chronic known issue
Add an optional one-question IVR CSAT immediately after a support call resolves, distinct from the delayed email survey
Route a confirmed recurring theme to the brand brain and the relevant specialist, never just a report that sits unread
outputs: a theme-clustered VoC report with quote counts
trigger: monthly VoC review, or after a support call for the IVR check

external_write.surface: IVR platform for the post-call CSAT prompt

founder_sees: the theme list with quotes and counts

name: EXTENSION: Detect drift between support macros/knowledge base and current product, policy and price
what: The original capability writes reply templates and tagging/routing rules. It did not include checking that those templates stay true after a price change, a policy change, or a product going out of stock or discontinued, which is how a support macro ends up promising something the brand no longer offers.
encompasses: Extract every claim a macro or canned reply makes about price, policy, stock or timeline
Check each claim against the current brand record on a schedule
Flag a macro that now contradicts the current policy or price, with the specific line and the current correct value
Never auto-edit a macro; hand the flagged list to the support lead to fix
Re-run the check after every policy or price change event, not only on a fixed schedule
outputs: a drift report listing outdated macros and the correction needed
trigger: after any policy or price change, and monthly otherwise
founder_sees: the drift report

name: EXTENSION: Design a formal paid ambassador/affiliate tier alongside the give-X-get-X referral program
what: The original capability designs a give-X-get-X referral program and finds non-competing partner perks. It did not cover a formal paid ambassador or affiliate tier with tracked commission, which agencies and tools (creator-seeding, commission-tracking platforms) sell as a distinct program from peer referral.
encompasses: Design a tiered commission structure by ambassador cohort value (a repeat buyer vs a content creator with reach)
Set the tracking mechanism (unique code or link) and the commission-payment cadence
Write the seeding process: who gets approached, what they receive, what content or promotion is expected
Keep this program's economics separate from the give-X-get-X referral program's economics so the two are not double-counted
Set a cap or approval gate on total commission payout per period
outputs: an ambassador/affiliate program design with commission tiers and payout cap
trigger: the referral program is mature and the brand wants a more formal paid layer
founder_sees: the tier structure and the payout cap before launch

name: EXTENSION: Coordinate loyalty-point incentives for reviews without violating platform rules
what: The original capability times and words review requests and drafts responses. It did not cover coordinating with the loyalty program when points are offered for leaving a review, which is allowed for on-site reviews but forbidden by Google and by Amazon/marketplace terms for their own reviews, a distinction that is easy to get wrong.
encompasses: Check which review destinations in a given request may be incentivised (own site: usually yes) and which may not (Google, Amazon, most marketplaces: no)
Route the loyalty-point incentive only to the review destinations it is allowed on
Word the review request so a marketplace or Google-bound ask never mentions a reward
Flag any existing incentive wording found to violate a platform's terms, since this risks account suspension, not just a warning
Keep the incentive budget (points cost) visible to the founder against the review volume it buys
outputs: a flag list of any current violation
trigger: setting up or auditing the review request program
founder_sees: the flag list and the corrected rule
human_role: review platform manager / loyalty program manager

name: EXTENSION: Add a failed-delivery win-back variant, distinct from an ordinary lapsed-buyer win-back
what: The original capability builds the win-back flow for a lapsed customer and the sunset flow. It treated every lapsed customer the same. A customer whose order was never delivered (a carrier return-to-sender, or in India an RTO) needs a trust-rebuilding message, not a discount-led win-back, since the reason they stopped buying was a delivery failure, not fading interest.
encompasses: Detect a delivery-failure-caused lapse (return-to-sender for US carriers, RTO for India) separately from an ordinary engagement-decay lapse
Lead the message with an apology and a fix (address confirmation, a named contact, proof the issue is resolved) rather than a discount
Confirm the address and carrier serviceability before re-targeting the customer with any offer
Only offer a discount as a second step, after trust is addressed, and size it to the disruption, not to a generic win-back rate
Track win-back rate for the delivery-failure-affected segment separately from the ordinary lapsed segment, since mixing them hides whether the fix worked
inputs: carrier delivery-exception / return-to-sender event log (RTO/NDR event log for India)
ordinary lapse/churn flag from the segmentation model
outputs: a separate win-back rate for the delivery-failure-affected segment
trigger: a customer's most recent order shows a delivery-failure event (return-to-sender, or RTO/NDR for India) before the standard win-back trigger fires
tools: carrier delivery-exception data (or RTO data, for India) (read)
founder_sees: the message variant and the separate win-back rate

name: EXTENSION: Add reward-optimisation analytics to loyalty and VIP tier design
what: The original capability builds the flows that fire off loyalty-app events and defines VIP program rules. It did not include using redemption-behaviour analytics to decide which rewards to add, keep or retire, which loyalty platforms now surface as a distinct, data-driven step rather than a one-time reward-menu design.
encompasses: Track redemption rate and time-to-redeem per reward in the current menu
Flag a reward nobody redeems as a candidate to retire, freeing its point cost for something else
Flag a reward that redeems fast and often as a candidate to expand into a higher tier or feature more
Model the point-liability change before adding or removing a reward, since points are a real liability, not a free lever
Bring the founder a short list of add/keep/retire recommendations with the redemption evidence, not a full program rewrite
outputs: a reward add/keep/retire recommendation with redemption evidence
trigger: quarterly loyalty program review
founder_sees: the recommendation list and the liability model
